info.name: E-Commerce Platform API v1 (Requirements 1 + 2)
info.description:
REST API documentation and proof tests.

Base URL: {{base_url}} (API version v1 in the path).
Run order in the Collection Runner: 0 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5. Folder 1 needs OTP codes, folder 6 needs Docker changes (see each request's description).

Every error uses the unified format {"status", "code", "message"} (+ "errors" for validation, + "details" for extra data).

item.name: 0 - Setup (run first: logs in the 3 seeded accounts)
1 - Auth
item.description:
Register / verify use an OTP code that is written to storage/logs/laravel.log (MAIL_MAILER=log). Get it with:
docker compose exec app sh -c "grep -a 'Your code is' storage/logs/laravel.log | tail -n 1"
then put it in the collection variable otp_code.

item.name: Verify email (put OTP in otp_code first)

request.description: Manual: set the collection variable otp_code to the code from the log. Returns 200 + access_token, or 422 if the code is wrong/expired.
Before verification the login is refused with 403 'Please verify your email first.'

item.name: Reset password (put OTP in otp_code first)

request.description: Manual: use the reset code from the log. Keeps the same password so the other requests keep working.

exec: pm.test("All products are in Audio", () => pm.response.json().data.forEach(p => pm.expect(p.category).to.eql("Audio")));
pm.test("Sorted by price descending", () => pm.expect(prices).to.eql([...prices].sort((a, b) => b - a)));

item.name: Product details (+ stock from inventory over gRPC)

exec: pm.test("Has stock info from the inventory service", () => pm.expect(p).to.have.property("stock"));

item.name: My orders (customer sees only his own)

exec: pm.test("Contains the order just created", () => pm.expect(me.map(o => o.id)).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("customer_order_id")));
pm.test("Got notifications about the order", () => pm.expect(list.length).to.be.above(0));

item.name: 4 - Requirement 2: Inventory over gRPC
item.description: Every request here goes from Laravel to the Node.js inventory service over gRPC.

item.name: Order 2 units of product 2 (one gRPC reservation for all items)
Stock of product 1 before rejected order
Insufficient stock - rejected with clear message (409)

exec: pm.test("Message explains the shortage", () => pm.expect(json.message).to.include("Not enough stock"));

item.name: All-or-nothing: product 1 was not taken by the rejected order
5 - PROOF Requirement 1 (access is refused)
item.description: Run with the Collection Runner after folders 0 and 3. Every request must be refused.

item.name: Customer2's order list does not contain customer's order

exec: pm.test("Other users' orders are hidden", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.map(o => o.id)).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("customer_order_id")));

item.name: Login brute force -> 429 (repeats itself up to 6 times)

request.description: Repeats automatically in the Collection Runner until the API answers 429 Too Many Requests (limit: 5 login attempts per minute). Wait one minute afterwards before logging in again.

item.name: 6 - PROOF Requirement 2 (failure scenarios - follow each description)
item.description: These need a change in Docker before sending. Race condition: run  docker compose exec inventory node scripts/race-test.js

item.name: A) Inventory stopped -> create order gives 503 with clear message

request.description:
BEFORE: docker compose stop inventory
Expected: 503 'The inventory service is currently unavailable...' immediately (no waiting), no order created.
AFTER: docker compose start inventory

item.name: B) Inventory stopped -> product details still work, stock unavailable

request.description: Same state as A (inventory stopped). Expected: 200, product shown, stock.available_quantity = null with a message.

item.name: C) Inventory too slow -> 504 after the 2 s deadline

request.description:
BEFORE (PowerShell): $env:INVENTORY_DELAY_MS=5000; docker compose up -d inventory
Expected: 504 after ~2 seconds (not 5), message 'did not respond within 2000 ms'. Stock unchanged.
AFTER: $env:INVENTORY_DELAY_MS=0; docker compose up -d inventory

exec: pm.test("Answered at the deadline, not after 5 s", () => pm.expect(pm.response.responseTime).to.be.below(4000));

item.name: D1) Stock of product 5 before failed save
D2) Save fails after reservation -> 500, stock returned

request.description:
BEFORE: in src/.env set SIMULATE_ORDER_SAVE_FAILURE=true then  docker compose exec app php artisan config:clear
Expected: 500 'The order could not be saved. The reserved stock was returned to the inventory.'
AFTER: set it back to false and run config:clear again.

exec: pm.test("Same stock as before the failed order", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.stock.available_quantity).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("stock_before_fail"))));
